title: Pickleball Unforced-Error Rate by Session
dataSources: Bar-velocity reps (`vbt:rep`), sprint reps (`sprint:rep`), serve attempts (`serve:attempt`), pickleball rallies (`pickleball:rally`), swim sets (`swim:set`), archery ends (`archery:end`), balance trials (`balance:trial`), and batting reps (`batting:rep`).
app: Sports and skill telemetry from VBT devices, sprint timers, serve trackers, swim logs, archery apps, balance trainers, and batting sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=pickleball:rally
| stats count as rallies sum(eval(if(result="unforced_error",1,0))) as errors by session_id
| eval error_pct=round(100*errors/rallies,1)
| sort - error_pct
description: Calculates the share of rallies ending in your own unforced errors for each session.
value: A simple unforced-error rate gives skill practice a clean number to improve even without full match analytics.
implementation: Label rally outcomes from a scoring app or practice notebook and aggregate them by session.
visualization: Bar chart of unforced-error percentage by session.
grandmaExplanation: It logs how often your own mistakes are ending pickleball rallies in each practice or match session.
